module purpose: Bridge between JTAG TAP and the RISC-V Debug Module Interface (DMI): synchronize JTAG inputs, run the TAP state machine and IR/DR access logic (IDCODE, DTMCS, DMI, bypass), and implement a DMI controller that turns DR updates into outward dmi_req_o requests and consumes dmi_rsp_i responses.

use-case flows.value: write DTMCS fields (including dmireset and dmihardreset) into the DTMCS register
start a DMI request: latch op/addr/wdata from the DMI DR into the controller and assert busy
drive the external DMI request outputs (op, addr, data) and handle the DMI response (rdata/ack)
shift/read out selected register bits to JTAG TDO (IDCODE / DTMCS / DMI / bypass / IR)
return DMI read data from dmi_rsp_i into the DMI DR (rdata -> dmi_ctrl.rdata -> tap_reg.dmi_nxt -> tap_reg.dmi captured for JTAG)
the busy flag that blocks acceptance of new DMI requests while a request is outstanding
clear TAP registers and DMI controller state on external reset (rstn_i)

conceptual assets.concept: DMI transaction (operation, address, write-data) as shifted in via the DMI DR and transmitted to the external DMI interface
conceptual assets.reasoning: The DMI payload bits are shifted into and captured in tap_reg.dmi (DR_SHIFT / DR_CAPTURE at lines 192-197 and 185-189). When the DR update event is present (dr_trigger.valid) and the instruction register selects the DMI register, the dmi_controller latches address, write-data and operation from tap_reg.dmi into dmi_ctrl.addr / dmi_ctrl.wdata / dmi_ctrl.op and asserts busy to start a request (lines 161, 263-271). Those controller fields are exported on the external request port (dmi_req_o.addr/data/op) (lines 283-285). Corruption of these values would change the operation the consumer receives; the map records show the concrete connections (dmi_req_o.* COPIES dmi_ctrl.* at their occurrence ids, and tap_reg.dmi SOURCES the controller fields).

conceptual assets.concept: DTMCS configuration bits (including dmireset and dmihardreset) that control DMI resets and status
conceptual assets.reasoning: The module composes tap_reg.dtmcs_nxt (lines 219-226) and stores it into tap_reg.dtmcs on DR_CAPTURE (line 188). When a DR update event targets the DTMCS register, the dmi_controller copies the DTMCS bits into dmi_ctrl.dmireset and dmi_ctrl.dmihardreset (lines 247-251), which in turn control error clearing and gating of DMI operations (lines 256-266). The map shows tap_reg.dtmcs_nxt COPIES the controller reset bits and tap_reg.dtmcs is CLOCKED_BY clk_i, giving concrete structural references.

conceptual assets.concept: Instruction register value (IREG) that selects which IR/DR is active and thus which register is read/written
conceptual assets.reasoning: The IREG value is loaded on IR_CAPTURE/IR_SHIFT (lines 178-181) and the design uses it to select which register is captured/shifted/read on DR states and which data appear on TDO (lines 185-197, 202-211). Corrupting IREG changes which register is accessed; the map shows tap_reg.ireg is a clocked register (CLOCKED_BY clk_i) and it is the selector for the DR/IR logic.

conceptual assets.concept: JTAG TDO output (serial readout) that reports the selected register contents off-chip
conceptual assets.reasoning: On TCK falling edges the module drives jtag_tdo_o with either the IR bit (in IR_SHIFT) or the selected DR bit (IDCODE/DTMCS/DMI/bypass) (lines 202-211). The integrity objective that external observers receive the register bits implemented by the selected register is established by these assignments. The map shows jtag_tdo_o derivations and selections from tap_reg.idcode / tap_reg.dtmcs / tap_reg.dmi / tap_reg.bypass.

conceptual assets.concept: DR-update trigger (dr_trigger.valid) that enables use of captured DR contents (the update event)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The two-bit shift register dr_trigger.sreg captures DR_UPDATE events in the update_trigger process and dr_trigger.valid is asserted when sreg="01" (lines 151-156, 161). The DMI controller and DTMCS logic use dr_trigger.valid to permit copying of tapped-in values into controller state (lines 247-265). The map shows dr_trigger.sreg as a clocked register (CLOCKED_BY clk_i) and dr_trigger.valid computed from sreg (GATED_BY at its occurrence).

conceptual assets.concept: DMI controller busy flag that blocks new request acceptance until the outstanding DMI completes
conceptual assets.reasoning: The busy register is asserted by the controller when it begins handling a DMI op (lines 269-271) and is the gate that prevents new request setup (lines 263-266, 270-271). If busy is corrupted the controller could incorrectly accept or reject requests; the map shows dmi_ctrl.busy is a clocked register (CLOCKED_BY clk_i) and used as a control-only source that gates address/op/wdata updates and response handling.

conceptual assets.concept: DMI controller error indicator (dmi_ctrl.err) and its inclusion in readback
conceptual assets.reasoning: The controller sets err on certain conditions (line 259) and clears it on reset or on DMI reset (lines 256-258). The readback into the DMI DR encodes err bits (tap_reg.dmi_nxt includes replicate_f(dmi_ctrl.err,2) at line 229), so err's integrity affects what the host reads. The map shows dmi_ctrl.err is a clocked register and that tap_reg.dmi_nxt DERIVES_FROM dmi_ctrl.err (occurrence/records cited in the structural references).
